financial_flags.finding: Revenue has declined two years in a row (2.70B → 2.49B → 2.446B).
financial_flags.why: Profitability was reached through cost cuts rather than growth; the top line is still shrinking.

financial_flags.finding: Total liabilities (2.196B) exceed total assets (2.056B) at FY2026 year-end.
financial_flags.why: Implies a stockholders' deficit, which limits balance sheet cushion, though the gap narrowed from FY2025 (2.539B liabilities vs 2.125B assets).

financial_flags.finding: Long-term debt of 1.33B against cash of 1.2066B; interest expense was cited at 123.8M and 134.5M in two periods.
financial_flags.why: Heavy fixed interest burden relative to the thin net income of 63.2M.

financial_flags.finding: Positive turnaround: net income of 63.2M in FY2026 versus losses of 118.9M and 551.9M; cash up from 697.6M to 1.2066B over two years; debt down from 1.549B.
financial_flags.why: The trend is improving, but one profitable year is a short track record.

risks.finding: Profitability is new and may not be sustained; the company has a history of large operating losses.
risks.evidence_quote: Although we reported net income in fiscal year 2026, we have incurred significant operating losses in prior periods

risks.finding: About $1.3B of debt (Term Loan plus $350M 5.50% convertible notes due 2029). Credit agreement covenants include a $1.2B subscription revenue test and $250M minimum liquidity when the revolver is drawn.
risks.evidence_quote: to maintain Subscription Revenue of the company and its subsidiaries of at least $1.2 billion for the four-quarter trailing period

risks.finding: Ongoing class actions, personal injury claims and government inquiries tied to Tread+ and Bike recalls. A new Bike+ recall was announced in November 2025.
risks.evidence_quote: In November 2025, in collaboration with the CPSC and Health Canada, we announced a voluntary recall of certain Original Series Bike+ units

risks.finding: The company has been named in securities class actions and stockholder derivative suits.
risks.evidence_quote: We have been named in securities class action lawsuits and stockholder derivative actions

risks.finding: Material weaknesses were identified in FY2021–FY2024. They are described as previously identified and remediated, but could recur, for example around inventory counts with last-mile partners.
risks.evidence_quote: we identified certain material weaknesses in our internal control over financial reporting

risks.finding: Demand forecasting and inventory risk: past write-downs, discounting and disputes with suppliers over purchase commitments.
risks.evidence_quote: We have in recent periods experienced, and may continue to experience decreases in consumer demand, resulting in inventory write-downs

risks.finding: Sole reliance on contract manufacturers, often a single supplier, concentrated in Taiwan, China and Thailand. Tariffs are also a risk.
risks.evidence_quote: We are solely reliant on contract manufacturers for all of our manufacturing needs.

red_flags.evidence_quote: We have been and in some cases continue to be subject to class action litigation, private personal injury claims and other regulatory proceedings

rating_rationale: Peloton has improved: FY2026 net income was 63.2M, cash was 1.2066B and debt fell. Management concluded ICFR was effective (9A-p005), and no going-concern language turned up in the searches. Offsetting this: revenue has fallen two years running, liabilities exceed assets, about 1.3B of debt carries covenants, there is continuing product-safety litigation and recall exposure, and material weaknesses were reported in FY2021–FY2024. The material weakness flag is marked not_found because the weaknesses are described as previously identified and remediated. This is research, not investment advice.
open_questions: Read Note 12 (Commitments and Contingencies) for the size of accruals and potential exposure from the Tread+/Bike/Bike+ recall litigation and the securities class actions.
Confirm that the earlier material weaknesses are fully remediated, and check how the shift to a shared-services provider (9A-p008) affects controls.
Check the quality of FY2026 earnings: restructuring, impairment and stock-based compensation effects, and free cash flow.
Review the subscription revenue trend against the $1.2B covenant threshold and the 2029 debt maturity wall.
Confirm that the auditor (Ernst & Young) has not changed. No change was found in the sections searched, but Item 9 was not reviewed.
